Named for his father. Second of the four Roos children on the 1902 notice.

Named on the 1902 notice as Anna Francisa Roos's husband, married in community of property. The only son-in-law on the page.

Two sons documented: Hendrik Stephanus Nicolaas, baptised 1882, and Diederik Arnoldus, born about August 1887.

s: c. Aug 1887, Zwartruggens – 1 Mar 1935, Voorbedacht No. 401, district Rustenburg · Booyzen
x: A KARWEIER — a transport rider — of Zwartruggens, and a son of Ockert Johannes Stephanus Booysen and Elizabeth Johanna Sophia Myburgh. The fourth generation to carry the name that came into this family with Anna Catharina Johanna Olivier, whose father was Ocken Johannes Oliefier of the district of Cradock. Named on his father’s 1935 Sterfkennis as a minor of seven.

s: 4 Jan 1882, Rustenburg – 8 Oct 1959, Kempton Park — buried 12 Oct, Roodepoort–Maraisburg · Booyzen
x: Baptised at Rustenburg on 30 January 1882, son of Ockert Johannes Stephanus Booysen and Elisabetta Johanna Sophia Myburgh — and named for his uncle, who was then twenty and would be dead at Brakfontein before the boy turned ten. He outlived that uncle by sixty-eight years.
Married in community of property to Willem Grobelaar, in whose house at Koedoesfontein her father died.
Married in community of property to Stephanus Andries Venter.

Baptised at Rustenburg in 1889, son of Petrus Jacobus Booijsen and Anna Catharina Sofia Benadi. The fifth Petrus Jacobus, and the name has now run five generations without a break.

Baptised at Rustenburg on 4 November 1894, son of Petrus Jakobus Booysen and Anna Catharina Sophia Benadie — named for his uncle, who was named for HIS mother’s father, Ocken Johannes Oliefier of the district of Cradock. Three generations of a name that came into this family with one marriage.
Eighth and last on the 1876 notice, named for her mother Anna Maria van der Merwe.

s: 10 Sep 1824, baptised 4 Oct 1824 at Cradock – 9 May 1891, Brakfontein, district Rustenburg · Booyzen
x: THE FIRST WIFE OF HENDRIK STEFANUS BOOIJSEN, and for a week this archive had her filed as a stranger. Her own Sterfkennis 6332 gives her parents as OCKEN JOHANNES OLIEFIER and ANNA JOHANNA BOTHA, her age as 67 years 8 months and 1 day, her farm as BRAKFONTEIN — which this archive read as Boekfontein — and her surname as OLIEFIER, which this archive read as Alberts. She was still married when she died: her husband outlived her by seventeen years and remarried at Zeerust eleven months later. Seven children, all of age: Petrus Jacobus, Ocken Johannes, Anna Johanna Maria, Elesabettha Maria Cornelya, Alettha Catrina Johanna, Magdalena Johanna, Hendrick Stefanus Nicolaas. Her father is where OCKERT JOHANNES came into this family — and her 1824 baptism gives his name entire, OCKERT JOHANNES STEPHANUS OLIVIER, which is exactly what her son was called. She married Hendrik Stephanus Booijzen at POTCHEFSTROOM on 3 JULY 1850, entry 206, she 25 and he 23 — the earliest evidence this archive has of this family north of the Vaal, twenty-six years before the 1876 death at Rustenburg and two years before the Sand River Convention.

s: c. 31 Jan 1862, district Rustenburg – 14 May 1891, Brakfontein, district Rustenburg · Booyzen
x: Dead at twenty-nine on his father's farm, FIVE DAYS AFTER HIS MOTHER, and unknown to this archive until his notice was read. He is the seventh child on his mother's list and the first Booysen this archive has documented as BORN in the Transvaal.

Named with his wife Anna Johanna Botha on line 3 of their daughter's 1891 Sterfkennis, and the reason a Booysen grandson was called OCKERT JOHANNES STEPHANUS. He is the head of a line this archive has not worked at all.

s: 25 Jul 1820, baptised 2 Oct 1820 at Cradock – — · Olivier

Named as her daughter's mother on the 1891 Sterfkennis. A fourth Botha marriage in this archive, and none of them yet joined to another.

Third of the seven children on the 1891 Sterfkennis, of age by then and not traced since. She is not the Anna Catharina Grobelaar of the 1908 notice — the forenames do not agree — and this archive has not settled whether they are the same woman.
Fourth of the seven children on the 1891 Sterfkennis. Of age by 1891, and absent from her father's 1908 notice, which names only four children — so she probably died in between.

s: 1 Jun 1901, Cape Province – 11 Dec 1947, Forest Hill — West Park, D.R., grave 2171 · Booyzen

Fourth on the 1863 list, and THE DIRECT ANCESTOR'S BROTHER — Willem Hermanus is sixth on the same list. For the whole of this project he was a line on that list and nothing else. His wife's 1900 death notice gives him a household: married ELIZABETHA MARGARETHA MARAIS at LADY GREY, the same small Cape church where his brother married Kathleen Barry in 1879; eight children; and by 1900 he was at Pretoria, living in a zinc building in Market Street. He signed her notice there in March 1904 — and on 27 NOVEMBER 1905 he married again at Pretoria, to JOHANNA ELENA STOLS, widow Lowies, of Skinners Court. He was 56, a widower of GOEDE HOOP, PRETORIA, and the register gives his birthplace as CRADOCK. The Remarks column cites his remarriage certificate from the Master, NO. 4795 — which is the number of his first wife’s death notice, so the two documents point at each other and the identification needs no inference. His own death is still not found.

His second wife, married at Pretoria on 27 November 1905 — she 51 and a WIDOW LOWIES of Skinners Court, he 56 and a widower of Goede Hoop. Her first husband was CHARLES PETRUS BAREND LOWIES, born in the district of Cradock about 1849 and dead at Pretoria on 5 JUNE 1905 — FIVE MONTHS AND TWENTY-TWO DAYS before she married again. Estate 7081, which the marriage register cites beside his 4795. TWELVE children by Lowies, SIX OF THEM STILL MINORS when he died — and her second husband lived at the same address, GOEDEHOOP. She signed her first husband’s death notice on 27 October 1905 and married her second on 27 November.

s: c. Oct 1848, district Cradock – 5 Jun 1905, the Lunatic Asylum, Pretoria · Booyzen

He was a HAWKER, of GOEDEHOOP, PRETORIA — which is the exact address David Schalk Booyzen gave on the marriage register three weeks later, so the two men lived in the same place. Dutch, of the Cradock district, 56 years and 8 months, dead in the LUNATIC ASYLUM at Pretoria on 5 June 1905. Movables but no land, an estate over £100, and a will. Six of the twelve children were still minors. His widow signed the notice on 27 October and married David Schalk on 27 November.

s: c. May 1874, Middelburg – 31 Mar 1930, Church Street, Middelburg · Booyzen

s: c. 20 Mar 1754, “this Colony” – 16 Jun 1843, 28 Roze Street, Cape Town · Booyzen

Widow of Charles du Plessis; one daughter, married to Benjamin Solomon; “no property whatever except a Bond amounting per balance to £15”. Line 3 answers “both dead”. She is here because she was born in 1754 and died in 1843 — the only two dates this archive has for Magdelena Elisabeth de Beer, both off the family tree with no source stated — and because somebody will one day find her and decide she is the same woman. She is not. Her name is not Magdelena, not Elisabeth, and not de Beer.

The second wife of Petrus Jacobus Booysen, named at last from the 1870 baptism of her son Gert Jacobus — not from any death notice, none of which would give her. Mother of Gert Jacobus (1870) and, with the tree's misattributions corrected, of Izak (1864) and Stephanus Francois (1874).
Third witness at the 1870 font, and presumably the bride's people — the only trace the archive has of Johanna Margaritha Pretorius's own family.

s: c. 1886 – 29 Jul 1932, Johannesburg Hospital — buried Brixton, grave 6889 · Booyzen
x: AN EIGHTH CHILD, and one this archive did not have. Confirmed at Indwe on 31 May 1907, aged 21, entered “Booijzen”. A MIJNWERKER of DUGMORE MIJN when he married Susanna Adriana Roodt, 16, at Indwe on 21 September 1908 — the only miner in five generations of read occupations, and the answer to the last line of the family testimony. Two children in nine months by two women of the same surname, both entered “onecht”. His mother stood godmother at the first font, which is how this archive knows whose son he is. AND THEN JOHANNESBURG: a WILLIAM HERMAN BOOYZEN, 47, born Cape Province, married, EX MINER UNDERGROUND, of 62 Langford Street, Booysens, died at Johannesburg Hospital on 29 July 1932 of a perforated duodenal ulcer after about one day, and was buried at BRIXTON on 31 July. The occupation, the province, the age within a year and the cemetery all fit; no parents are named, because a civil registration does not ask. And then the grave register closes it: GRAVE 6889 holds “Boysen, William” and, thirty-six years later, SUSANNA ADRIANA BOOYZEN, buried 29 August 1968 — the woman he married at Indwe in 1908. Husband and wife in one grave.

s: c. 1892 – buried 29 Aug 1968, Johannesburg — grave 6889 · Booyzen
x: SIXTEEN when she married at Indwe on 21 September 1908, with her parents consenting, and already the mother of a son born on 31 May. She outlived her husband by thirty-six years and was buried in his grave — number 6889, Johannesburg — on 29 August 1968.

Seventeen at the same confirmation, number 25 on the page to Susanna Adriana’s 26. Mother of the girl born 8 February 1909 — four and a half months after he married the other one. The register names her plainly and this archive does no more than repeat it.

Baptised at Indwe 22 September 1910, entry 12, entered ONECHT and GRATIS — the fee waived. Named for her godmother Catharina Willemina Levina Buitendag, who stood at both of her father’s children’s fonts.
Godmother at Indwe in 1908 and again in 1910, to two children of the same father by two different mothers — and the second child carries her whole name.
Godfather at both Indwe fonts. A Cornelis de Klerk Roodt, 21, is number 29 in the same 1907 confirmation class; whether they are the same man is not established here.

Carries the Kolbe name three generations after the 1820 Settler.

s: c. 1887 – 8 Dec 1956, Florence Nightingale Nursing Home — buried 12 Dec, grave 7110/1 · Booyzen
x: A son of Willem Hermanus and Kathleen Barry. This archive had him as a name on Transvaal estate MHG 10/57 and nothing else — not a birth, not a death. The Johannesburg cemetery register gives all of it: DIED 8 DECEMBER 1956 at the FLORENCE NIGHTINGALE NURSING HOME of CORONARY PULMONARY SCLEROSIS, aged 69, usual residence 3 15TH AVENUE, MAYFAIR — the same suburb where his mother died in 1940 and where his great-niece was married at St Joseph’s in 1949. Buried 12 December in the D.R. section, GRAVE 7110/1, a double plot. In 1912 he married Dorothea Regina Barry, a daughter of his mother's brother Hendrik Nicholaas — the third Barry–Booyzen union in three generations.

s: c. 1894, Cape of Good Hope – 25 Oct 1918, Turffontein — buried 27 Oct, Brixton, D.R., grave 1119 · Booyzen

Not a family place — a trap. Booysens is a mining suburb south of the Johannesburg city centre, a couple of miles from Forest Hill and Kenilworth where this family actually lived in the 1940s. The farm where the oldest document in this archive was written. On 14 September 1876, thirteen days after the death, somebody at Brakfontein filled in Sterfkennis No. 678 for Petrus Jacobus Booijsen, aged 88, and wrote the names of his parents on line 3. Fifteen years later it takes two more: his son's wife on 9 May 1891 and their son five days after her. And in 1892 Hendrik Stefanus, marrying again at Zeerust, still gives Brakfontein as his home — sixteen years on the same ground. The coordinates are approximate: the district is certain, the farm is not yet placed.

Where this family's western Transvaal branch is, and it is a branch rather than a lead now. Jan Gerthardus Lodewikus Booijsen — fifth of the eight children on the 1876 Sterfkennis, born district Graaff-Reinet about 1818 — died on the farm Vaalbank in this district on 25 May 1885, estate TAB MHG O/2899. His daughter Magdalena Susanna Maria died on the same farm on 1 May 1920, and her Sterfkennis names him. Lichtenburg is one district west of Rustenburg, where his father died in 1876, and one district east of Marico.

Where a Booyzen worked underground. The Indwe marriage register of 21 September 1908 gives both bride and groom's dwelling place as “Dugmore Mijn” and the groom's trade as “Mijnwerker”. It is the only mine anywhere in this archive attached to a named member of this family, and it is coal in the Cape rather than gold on the Rand. The coordinates are approximate — the workings were at Indwe and the exact site is not yet fixed.

One farm, two deaths, thirty-five years apart, and the same family on it both times. Jan Gerthardus Lodewikus Booijsen — born district Graaff-Reinet about 1818, fifth child on the 1876 Sterfkennis — died here on 25 May 1885. His daughter Magdalena Susanna Maria, born about 1860, died here on 1 May 1920. It is the clearest evidence this archive has that the family did not merely pass through the western Transvaal but settled in it, two generations before anyone reached Johannesburg. The coordinates are approximate: the district is certain, the farm is not yet placed.

The third named Barry farm, after Manorowen and Jerpoint. Harriet Louisa Barry, eighteen, died here of typhoid on 7 September 1912 after thirty days' illness and was carried back to Manorowen to be buried. Her father, who signed the form, gave his own residence as Manorowen — so Cherryville is somewhere the family worked rather than lived, or another Barry household entirely. Where Dorothea Regina Barry, daughter of Hendrik Nicholaas Barry and Anna Johanna Maria Schoeman, was baptised on 3 April 1892. From the index rather than the register, and placed only approximately.

Where Hendrik Stephanus Booysen died on 11 May 1908, aged seventy-nine, in the house of his son-in-law Willem Grobelaar. A farmer with no movable property, some land, and mutual wills with both of his dead wives. Thirty-two years earlier he had signed his own father's Sterfkennis at Brakfontein, one district over.
